_note: Frozen content for design review. Instructional family — prose carries the page, the screen sits underneath as evidence rather than as the subject.
brief: Setting up a system that runs without you watching it

slots.eyebrow: Written down once, then left alone
slots.subtitle: Six pieces, each set up in an afternoon. Nothing clever, nothing that breaks when you go on holiday, and no step that depends on you remembering it.

slots.noteTitle: One database. Three views. Nothing else.
slots.line1: Create the database first and resist adding properties for a week.
slots.line2: Status, owner, date. Every view is a filter on those three, which is why three is enough.
slots.line3: Everything else is a page inside a row, not a new database — that is the mistake that turns this into work.

slots.noteTitle: If it cannot ship this week, cut it.
slots.line1: Scope is not ambition; it is how long you are willing to guess for.
slots.line2: One owner per item. Committees do not decide, they schedule, and the schedule is the delay.
slots.line3: Anything untouched for a week gets closed or halved. Nothing is allowed to quietly persist.

slots.toolTagline: How the money side is wired
slots.noteTitle: Check revenue once. Then close the tab.
slots.line1: One dashboard, opened in the morning and not again.
slots.line2: Payments and invoices run themselves; the only manual step left is deciding what to charge.
slots.line3: Failed charges retry on their own, which used to be an afternoon of chasing people.

slots.noteTitle: Never start from an empty page again.
slots.line1: Feed it enough of your own writing that the draft sounds like you on a good day.
slots.line2: Ask for three angles rather than one version, so you stop defending your first idea by default.
slots.line3: Check anything load-bearing. Fluency is not accuracy, and it will never flag the difference.

slots.noteTitle: Two piles: needs a decision, and everything else.
slots.line1: Most messages want a decision, not a reply, and sorting for that is the whole job.
slots.line2: Urgent and loud look identical here. Deadline pressure is real; social pressure is negotiable.
slots.line3: Anything longer than a paragraph belongs in the database, where it can still be found next month.

slots.noteTitle: Write down why, not only what.
slots.line1: Teams re-litigate settled decisions because nobody recorded the reasoning behind them.
slots.line2: One paragraph per decision is enough, and it has to be written the day it is made.
slots.line3: If you cannot say why, you will have the same discussion again within the quarter.

slots.body: The database first, because everything else eventually points at it. Give it an afternoon and leave the properties alone for a week.
slots.body2: A system you built in one sitting and never revisited is worth more than a perfect one you are still configuring in March.
slots.signoff: The afternoon is the entire cost
